routes.label: Use the equilateral center triangle and a vertical right triangle
Place the centers and use spatial distance equations

changes.rationale: The lower centers lie at height 1 and form an equilateral triangle of side 2, with circumradius 2/sqrt(3). The larger center is distance 3 from each lower center, so its upward displacement is sqrt(9-4/3)=sqrt(69)/3. Adding the lower height and upper radius gives 3+sqrt(69)/3, B. Reuse the revised C sphere-contact target and its complete synthetic-center and spatial-coordinate alternatives, but bind the current 903 full F-refined sphere definition without reverting it. This task uses only the external-contact and plane-contact portions. Exact h106 identifies sphere elements but does not supply those contact equations.

answerCheck.reason: The three lower centers lie at height 1 and form an equilateral triangle of side 2. Their common circumcenter is at horizontal distance 2/sqrt(3) from each. The large center must be above it with center distance 3 to each lower center, so its vertical rise is sqrt(9-4/3)=sqrt(69)/3. Its top is another radius 2 higher, giving 3+sqrt(69)/3.
